extra.message: The Flask session-signing key is hardcoded and publicly known. An attacker can forge session cookies, including Flask-Login identity data, and impersonate arbitrary users.

The attacker-controlled request.path is interpolated into a string before render_template_string evaluates it as Jinja. A crafted missing URL containing Jinja expressions causes server-side template injection and may permit code execution.

extra.message: The submitted registration code is interpolated directly into a textual SQL query passed to session.execute(). An attacker can alter the WHERE clause and bypass registration-code validation.
The search query parameter is interpolated into a raw SQL text() predicate. An attacker can inject SQL through the search parameter and alter the note query.
The route queries notes using the user_id supplied in the URL without requiring it to match current_user.id or excluding private notes. Any authenticated user can read another user's private notes.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The delete endpoint loads a note solely by attacker-controlled note_id and deletes it without checking note.user_id against current_user.id or requiring an administrator. Any authenticated user can delete any note.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: All non-password AccountForm fields, including attacker-submitted is_admin, are copied into current_user.__dict__. Any authenticated user can submit is_admin=true directly and grant themselves administrator privileges.

The profile-image URL supplied through the account form is passed directly to urlopen without restricting its host, address range, redirects, or scheme. An authenticated attacker can make the server request internal or otherwise protected resources.

A user-controlled URL is opened without a timeout and its entire response is read into memory without a size limit. A slow or arbitrarily large response can exhaust application workers or server memory.

The unsigned preferences cookie is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads during every request. An unauthenticated attacker can supply a malicious pickle payload and execute arbitrary code on the server.
User-controlled note text is rendered with Jinja's safe filter, disabling HTML escaping. A malicious note can execute persistent JavaScript when another user views the home page.

extra.message: The note text column is explicitly marked safe when rendering search results. Stored attacker-controlled HTML in a note is emitted without escaping and can execute JavaScript.

extra.message: The state-changing account endpoint uses a plain WTForms Form and performs no CSRF-token validation. An attacker can cause a logged-in victim to submit account changes, including password or administrator-status fields, from another site.
The database is seeded with predictable user/user and admin/admin credentials. If unchanged, remote attackers can authenticate directly, including as an administrator.
A fixed registration authorization code is embedded in the source and inserted into every empty database. Anyone with access to the code can use this predictable credential to create an account.
SQLAlchemy query echoing is unconditionally enabled. Executed statements and bound values, including email addresses and registration codes, are written to application logs.
